docRequirement: glossary.md:45 (§ Auto memory) binds the session-start load of the auto-memory index: "The first 200 lines or 25 KB of the `MEMORY.md` index loads at the start of every session." memory.md:384 states the same rule with the tie-break and the consequence: "The first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation. Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start." Two refinements bound to the same measurement: memory.md:388 — "The check measures only the content that loads: YAML frontmatter and block-level HTML comments are stripped before the index is loaded, so they don't count toward the limits"; and memory.md:390 — "This limit applies only to `MEMORY.md`. CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length", so the cap must NOT be applied to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md instruction layers or to `rules/*.md`. Two caps, both mandatory, whichever binds first: 200 lines AND 25 KB, measured on the stripped content.
current:
One of the two caps exists, and it is wired only on the route the product does not take.

- The only load-limit constant in the repo is `packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8` — `export const MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200;`. `grep -ran "MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT|25 \* 1024|25600|25_000"` over `packages/` and `apps/` returns three hits, all in `memory-store.ts` (:8, :29, :68), and no byte constant anywhere in the memory subsystem. The only byte constants in `packages/shared/src/agent/memory/` are `AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES = 256 * 1024` (`memory-cleanup.ts:33`, the scheduled rewrite pass's input guard) and `RULE_PATTERN_EXPANSION_BYTE_LIMIT` (`rule-matching.ts`, glob expansion) — neither is a load cap.
- `memory-store.ts:29-33` — `readMemoryFile(filePath, maxLines = MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT)` does `readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` and `.join('\n').trim()`. No byte measurement, no frontmatter or HTML-comment stripping.
- `readMemoryFileWithImports` (:66-110) threads `maxLines` through to each `@path` import; `loadMemoryPromptBlock` (:317-334) composes project/user/session `MEMORY.md` plus unscoped rules from those reads.
- That composer is the LEGACY route. `packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:453-455` — `const memoryContext = capabilityContextPinned ? '' : loadMemoryPromptBlock(workspaceRootPath, sessionId, {...})`. `capabilityContextPinned` is passed as `this.capabilityTurnRuntime !== null` by both live backends: `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6607` and `packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1257`. `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/storage-runtime-fork-memory.test.ts:11` records the same fact in prose — the flag "is TRUE on every normal Pi turn".
- The live route caps NOTHING. `MEMORY.md` is registered as a `kind: 'memory'` capability record at four sites in `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts`: global `join(configDir, 'MEMORY.md')` (:909-916, `configDir` = `~/.nessy-agent`, `packages/shared/src/config/paths.ts:18,21`), session (:977-986), project `.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md` (:1027-1034), project `MEMORY.md` (:1092-1099). `memoryFileRecords` (:369-435) records path, revision and content hash only — it never reads a bounded body; its one `readMemoryFile` call (:427) exists solely to discover `@import` lines.
- `packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:968-978` binds each record to a `RuntimeMemoryHandle` (:561-573: `key`, `resource`, `readOnly`, `format?: 'rule'`, `importParentPath?`) with no size field. `packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:218-219` — `case 'memory': memory.push(binding.memory);` — puts every one into `view.memory` with no filter.
- `packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:976-1015` (`composePinnedCapabilityContext`) iterates `runtime.view.memory` and at :977 does `const content = await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource)`. `packages/shared/src/capabilities/materializer.ts:169-185` native branch does `readFileSync(contentPath)`, checks revision/hash, and returns `content.toString('utf-8')` — the WHOLE file. For a non-rule layer :997 takes `body = content` verbatim; :1003-1008 strips only `@import` lines; :1014 pushes it into the pinned block, which `buildPinnedCapabilityContext` (:884-906) returns and every turn carries.
- No stripping of YAML frontmatter or block-level HTML comments happens on either route for a non-rule memory layer (`base-agent.ts:997` — `layer.format === 'rule' ? unscopedRuleBody(content) : content`). Frontmatter on `MEMORY.md` is not hypothetical: memory.md:394 documents Claude writing a `modified` frontmatter field into memory files.
- The existing test pins only the line cap on the legacy helper: `packages/shared/src/agent/memory/__tests__/memory-store.test.ts:47-58` — `it('caps prompt reads to 200 lines', ...)`, 250 lines in, 200 out. Nothing tests a byte cap, and nothing tests either cap through the pinned-context seam.
divergence:
Three deltas. None is a key rename — the 25 KB limit has no representation in the repo at all.

1. The byte cap does not exist. `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` (memory-store.ts:8) is the only load limit; there is no `MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT`, so "whichever comes first" (memory.md:384) cannot be evaluated. A 150-line `MEMORY.md` with long lines is under the line cap and over 25 KB, and loads whole on both routes.
2. The line cap that does exist is on the wrong route. It lives in `readMemoryFile` (memory-store.ts:29-33), reached only from `loadMemoryPromptBlock`, and `system.ts:453-455` skips that composer whenever the capability runtime is pinned — which `pi-agent.ts:6607` / `claude-agent.ts:1257` make true on every normal send. The shipped path (`base-agent.ts:976-1015` → `materializer.ts:169-185`) reads the file whole, so the observable behaviour on the live route contradicts memory.md:384's "Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start" outright: content beyond BOTH thresholds is loaded.
3. Measurement basis is wrong even where a cap runs. memory.md:388 requires frontmatter and block-level HTML comments to be stripped before the index is loaded and therefore before measurement; `readMemoryFile` measures raw lines and `base-agent.ts:997` passes non-rule content through unstripped, so a frontmatter block both consumes budget and reaches the model.

One thing is correct and must stay correct: memory.md:390 scopes the cap to `MEMORY.md` only. Instruction layers (`CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, `native-sources.ts:987-990`, :1088-1091) load in full today, which is what the doc asks; a fix must not cap them, and must not cap `rules/*.md` either.

change.what: Add `export const MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT = 25 * 1024;` beside `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT` (:8), citing glossary.md:45 and memory.md:384. Add one exported helper that is the single definition of "what loads": `export function capMemoryIndexLoad(raw: string, maxLines = MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT, maxBytes = MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT): string` — (a) strip a leading `---`-delimited YAML frontmatter block and block-level HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->` occupying whole lines) first, per memory.md:388; (b) take the first `maxLines` lines; (c) truncate to `maxBytes` UTF-8 bytes measured with `Buffer.byteLength`, cutting on a line boundary so a multi-byte character is never split; (d) `.trim()`. Give `readMemoryFile` an options parameter — `readMemoryFile(filePath, maxLines = MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT, options: { indexLimits?: boolean } = {})` — that routes through `capMemoryIndexLoad` when `indexLimits` is set and keeps today's line-only slice otherwise, because the same function is the `@import` scanner and the rule-file reader. In `readMemoryFileWithImports` pass `indexLimits` only at `state.depth === 0` (the index itself, :77), not to imports. In `loadMemoryPromptBlock` pass it for the three `MEMORY.md` reads (:326, :329, :330) and NOT for `loadUnscopedRuleMemories` (:328) — memory.md:390 scopes the cap to `MEMORY.md`.

blastRadius:
No wire and no persistence boundary — this is a read path only, `MEMORY.md` files are never rewritten by it, so it is NOT a risk trigger under AGENTS.md. What it does touch:

- `readMemoryFile` has 4 callers (codegraph): `memory-store.ts:77` (`readMemoryFileWithImports`) and `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:427` (the `@import` discovery scan). The second one is the sharp edge: what it discovers determines which `kind: 'memory'` records exist in the inventory, hence the capability generation and each record's `contentHash`, which `materializer.readText` re-checks at :180-183 and throws `stale()` on mismatch. Changing the scan changes the record SET, not just a body.
- `loadMemoryPromptBlock` has 3 callers, all in `packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts` (:453-455 is the live one). Capping there changes the legacy/unpinned prompt only.
- `base-agent.ts:976-1015` feeds two other things besides the prompt text: `eagerInstructionFiles` → `emitInstructionsLoaded` (:1043-1046), the documented `InstructionsLoaded` hook payload; and `pathScopedRules` (:984-996). A capped body that becomes empty hits the `continue` at :1008 and would SUPPRESS the `InstructionsLoaded` event for that file — keep the event tied to the file being loaded, not to the surviving body.
- The pinned block is part of Pi's cacheable system prefix (`packages/shared/AGENTS.md:50`), so its text changing invalidates the prompt cache once. Harmless, but it means both backends' first turn after the change re-primes.
- Server-side shapes only if the flag alternative is taken instead of the basename check: `NativeCapabilitySourceRecord` (`packages/shared/src/capabilities/types.ts:67-167`) and `RuntimeMemoryHandle` (`resolver.ts:561-573`). Neither is serialized to the renderer (`sourcePath` is documented server-only at types.ts:159), so even that variant stays in-process.
- Tests that read these seams: `packages/shared/src/agent/memory/__tests__/memory-store.test.ts:47`; `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/rules-unscoped-launch.test.ts` (harness and rule-path regression); `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/instructions-loaded.test.ts` and `nested-instruction-traversal.test.ts` (both call `buildPinnedCapabilityContext` through a `buildPinned()` shim); `packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/native-sources.test.ts` and `nested-instruction-discovery.test.ts` if the import scan is changed; `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/storage-runtime-fork-memory.test.ts`.
userImpact:
Latent on a fresh install, then silent and permanent once auto memory accumulates — and it degrades rather than errors, which is why nobody has reported it.

The growth is agent-driven and effectively unbounded: the `remember` tool appends one line per memory (`packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/remember.ts:90` → `memory-store.ts:122` `appendMemoryFile`), and the only sweep removes marked entries older than 30 days plus duplicates (`memory-cleanup.ts:31`, `AUTO_MEMORY_DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_DAYS = 30`) while skipping files over 256 KB entirely (:33). Nothing trims by line count or size.

Once a user's `~/.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md` passes 200 lines — weeks of ordinary use — EVERY session on the live path carries the whole file in its pinned block, line 201 onward included, where Claude would carry 200 lines. The user sees no message and no error; what they get is a smaller effective context window and earlier auto-compaction in long sessions, plus per-turn cost on a block that rides the cacheable prefix. There is no surface in the app that reports the loaded size, so the only symptom is "long chats compact sooner than they used to". The 25 KB half bites earlier for a memory file with long lines — 150 verbose entries clear 25 KB while staying under the line cap — and today neither limit fires.

The mirror-image case is real but not shipped: with the capability runtime OFF the legacy composer DOES cut at line 200, so a note the user put at line 250 is silently dropped. That route is not what a normal send takes (`pi-agent.ts:6607`, `claude-agent.ts:1257`), so treat it as a fallback-only hazard.

On this machine `~/.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md` does not exist yet (checked), so nothing is observable here today; it surfaces the moment auto memory is used for a few weeks.

(2) No real `MEMORY.md` on this machine exceeds either limit — `~/.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md` is absent — so the context-window cost is inferred from the code path, not measured. (3) Ownership of the frontmatter/HTML-comment stripping is ambiguous between this finding and f166 (the post-write over-limit error, memory.md:386, which is genuinely absent here — `grep -rna "read limit|over its read"` finds nothing): I put the stripping in the shared `capMemoryIndexLoad` helper because memory.md:388 defines the cap's measurement in terms of it, and f166's post-write check must measure the same way; if f166 lands first, that helper is the seam it should reuse rather than duplicate. (4) Whether capping the `native-sources.ts:427` import scan breaks an existing fixture in `capabilities/__tests__/nested-instruction-discovery.test.ts` — I read the discovery code but did not run those suites. (5) A related but distinct question I deliberately did not fold in: `memoryFileRecords` registers a `MEMORY.md`'s `@path` imports as their own eagerly-loaded layers, while memory.md says auto-memory topic files are read on demand and not loaded at startup — that is a separate divergence and needs its own finding, not this fix.
